Safety is our value: At Xella, we shape an appreciative safety culture, maintain open and cross-hierarchical communication, and jointly drive the continuous improvement of our processes and installations with a solution-oriented approach.

What you can expect!

We passionately care about the safety and health of everyone who works for or with us, because we know that every injury has an impact on their lives. safe work. safe life.

- As a Corporate EHS Manager, you will work hand in hand with our international executives and an international team of motivated EHS Managers and can rely on their support.

You will develop the competencies and soft skills of the responsible individuals in training and coaching sessions in order to continuously improve and strengthen our safety culture.

You can rely on this!

- Mobility: Company car also for private use and the option to lease a bicycle or e-bike at attractive rates.
- Well covered: We support you with a company pension scheme, group accident insurance and through the PME family service.
- Work out: Push yourself, not only at work, but also in our gym.
- 
This is what you bring!

- Being an EHS Manager is not just a job for you, but a passion with which you infect others?

- It would be an advantage if you have sound experience in occupational and plant safety from the manufacturing industry.

jobs.occupation: 206/2026 PhD/Postdoc position (m/f/d): AI for Safety-Critical Systems At the Autonomous Multisensor (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description:
At the Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg is following position available, subject to funding approval:

PhD/Postdoc position (m/f/d): AI for Safety-Critical Systems

At the Autonomous Multisensor Systems (AMS) group

Salary scale: 13 TV-L

Date commencing: as soon as possible

Duration: 24 months

Contract status: 100 %

The Autonomous Multisensor Systems Group at Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg develops advanced methods for sensor data processing and multisensor data fusion, with applications in autonomous mobility, robotics, and industrial process automation. Our research covers signal and image processing, state estimation, navigation, path planning, and machine learning.

Join our team and contribute to the new research project “Adaptive Safety Switching and Uncertainty-Responsive AI”, in which we develop innovative methods for the safe integration of artificial intelligence into safety-critical systems. You will investigate how sensor data can be used to reliably assess the state of a system, quantify the uncertainty of AI-based decisions, and enable safe switching between different operating modes. Your research will also address the verification and validation of hybrid AI systems, combining machine learning and probabilistic modeling with rigorous safety analysis.

More information about our group is available at ams.ovgu.de (https://ams.ovgu.de/) .

Job description:

Tasks:

- Conduct independent research on the safe integration of AI into safety-critical systems in close collaboration with the research team and project partner, addressing the research objectives below.
- Maintain regular communication and coordinate research activities with the project partner.
- Support project management activities and contribute to project reports.
- Document, publish, and present research results.

Research objectives:

- Analyze functional safety requirements and translate them into test scenarios, evaluation metrics, and data requirements.
- Develop and evaluate AI models for the sensor-based classification of safety-relevant operating states.
- Investigate and compare uncertainty quantification methods, including probabilistic models such as Gaussian process regression, ensemble methods, and conformal prediction.
- Define operating states and decision boundaries and develop safe switching strategies between AI-based and physics-based models.
- Investigate physics-informed machine learning approaches and their potential contribution to defining safe operating regions.
- Develop and evaluate safety-envelope and runtime-assurance concepts for hybrid AI systems.
- Investigate suitable verification and validation methods for the developed AI and hybrid-system concepts.

Requirements profile:

- M.Sc. (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, Systems Engineering or a closely related field.
- Good knowledge of machine learning, signal processing, data analysis, or related methods, and strong programming skills in Python and/or MATLAB.
- Excellent written and spoken English; German language skills are an advantage.
- Ability to conduct independent research and collaborate effectively with an interdisciplinary team and project partners.
- Strong interest in research combining AI, sensor data processing, and safety-critical systems.
- Willingness to publish research findings and present them at conferences.

Desirable qualifications:

- Knowledge of system identification and modeling.
- Knowledge of signal and sensor data processing and filtering techniques.
- Experience with machine learning, ideally including probabilistic models.
- Knowledge of uncertainty quantification methods.
- Familiarity with state estimation, safety-critical systems, or verification and validation methods is an advantage

Your benefits:

- The opportunity to pursue a Ph.D., supported by academic supervision and mentoring.
- A supportive, collegial team with an open culture of communication, where everyone’s voice is valued and initiative, creativity, and new ideas are welcome.
- Research support services and Graduate Academy programs to support your personal and professional development.
- An excellent working environment with a wide range of facilities on campus (canteen, further education opportunities, sports facilities, childcare, etc.).
- Attractive salary package according to TV-L (pay group 13) with occupational pension scheme (VBL) and 30 days of vacation per year

For further information about the position, please contact Prof. Benjamin Noack (benjamin.noack(at)ovgu.de)

You will benefit from our structures and offerings in the fields of sustainability, diversity, family support and staff development. Our location in the center of a thriving, lively and family-friendly state capital guarantees a high quality of life and a wide range of leisure activities. For more information, please visit www.ovgu.de/en/karriere (http://www.ovgu.de/en/karriere) .

Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg is a signatory of the German Diversity Charter. We welcome your application, regardless of gender, cultural and social background, age or sexual orientation. Applications from severely disabled people or people with an equivalent impairment will be given priority in the case of equal suitability, ability and professional expertise. Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg strongly promotes gender equality in all professional areas.

Please note the information for storage of personal data: https://www.ovgu.de/unimagdeburg/en/data_protection-p-66790.html (https://www.ovgu.de/unimagdeburg/en/data_protection-p-66790.html)

Please send your complete application (motivation letter, curriculum vitae, graduation certificates, references) by October 15, 2026 using the online application portal.

jobs.occupation: Doctoral researcher (m/f/d/x) in microbial systems biophysics (Biophysiker/in)
jobs.description:
Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.

The Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics at the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences, seeks to fill the above position.

About the position

- Salary group 13 TV-L 
- Fixed-term position in accordance with the training plan, initially for 1 year; an extension of the fixed-term contract is planned
- 50 % of a full-time position
- As soon as possible

The newly formed Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics (https://home.uni-leipzig.de/sysbiophys/) , led by Professor Katja Taute, is part of the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics (https://www.physes.uni-leipzig.de/en/pdi) , which hosts a broad range of biophysics research. Active matter, including bacterial systems, is a growing key research area at the Institute. Our research group develops and uses biophysical methods, including high-throughput, 3D bacterial tracking and microfluidics, in combination with theory and simulations, to quantitatively analyse the spatio-temporal dynamics of bacteria at the level of individuals and populations. One research focus is the chemotactic navigation of bacteria in mechanically complex environments. In nature, swimming bacteria navigate relative to chemical stimuli in environments ranging from open waters to soil and the gut.

The new doctoral researcher is to investigate how the gut bacterium E. coli navigates mechanically complex environments that mimic properties of its natural habitat. Properties of both the bacteria and the environment will be modulated in a controlled fashion to identify the underlying physical mechanisms and address the following questions:

- What is the relationship between behavioural and material parameters that enable optimal navigation?
- Is optimal intracellular information processing specific to the type of environment?
- How do bacteria navigate mechanical gradients?

The role

- Independent, original, experimental scientific research on the above project
- Additional scientific qualification (preparing a doctoral thesis)
- Thorough documentation of research

- Fluency in English at C1 level and in German; additional languages are an advantage

TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in the country. Research Associate / PostDoc (m/f/x)

starting January 1, 2027. The position is limited until February 29, 2028. The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz-WissZeitVG).

The candidate will be in charge of developing a novel generation of computing architectures based on ion computing. Development of novel switchable ultracapacitors and microsupercapacitors for iontronic applications, synthesis of porous carbon materials and porous membranes, development and adaption of new electrolyte formulations, electrochemical characterization, impedance spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, integration into a team of PhD and master students, scientific publishing, data management.

jobs.occupation: IMPACT EVALUATION, RESEARCH, AND LEARNING MANAGER (Maternity cover) (Fachangestellte/r - Markt- und Sozialforschung)
jobs.description:
OVERVIEW

Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.

For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. 

Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Beyond certification, Fairtrade International and its member organisations (three producer networks and 19 national Fairtrade organisations) partner with producers and businesses, engage consumers, and advocate for a fair and sustainable future.

Unit’s description and purpose: 

The Global Impact unit strengthens the Fairtrade system by driving institutional learning and effectiveness through robust monitoring and evaluation systems. We are the hub for the analysis and communication of high-quality data and information about Fairtrade and its impact, as well as supporting strategy delivery. The unit includes the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) team, which is the Fairtrade system’s hub for MEL which directly connects evidence to strategic decision for the Global Strategy, individual Fairtrade projects and global programmes, Standards, producer support, and more.

PRINCIPAL ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Overseeing Fairtrade Research and Evaluation: Manages Global Impact commissioned research and evaluations, and supports research and evaluations commissioned by other Fairtrade International units and Fairtrade organizations, ensuring that there are rigorous research methodologies, effective dissemination of findings, practical recommendations, and actionable learnings for the Fairtrade system. Develops and implements procedures and guidelines for the management of research and evaluations within the Fairtrade system.

Amplifying research findings internally and externally: Organizes learning events based on research to ensure learnings are promoted and used by various stakeholder groups within the Fairtrade system. Helps to build appropriate action-plans based on research where learnings are used to promote adaptation, change, and improvement. Presents Fairtrade research findings at external research workshops and conventions and helps to organize and facilitate presentations of others in the Fairtrade system. 

Encouraging a Fairtrade Learning Culture: Develops a Fairtrade Learning Strategy and adapts/maintains Fairtrade Research for Learning Agenda. Ensures that Fairtrade research contributes to understanding Fairtrade’s impact and tests the assumptions in Fairtrade’s Theory of Change. Coordinates research efforts across the Fairtrade system through the Research Task Force. Hosts and guides occasional research-focused interns, students from partner organisations, or student assistants.

Building External Research Collaborations: Builds on an existing academic engagement strategy to engage with external research institutions more deeply to collaboratively fund and perform research on Fairtrade’s impact. Brainstorms with external research teams, contributes to research funding proposals, builds research methodologies, jointly oversees research implementation, and works together to interpret, amplify, and communicate findings.

Managing Digital Learning Platforms: Acts as the product owner for Fairtrade’s Research Hub, a searchable database and platform of external studies exploring Fairtrade’s impact, and Fairlearn, a platform for live and asynchronous Fairtrade e-learning. Contributes to a Steering Committee for an Impact Platform for understanding and learning from Fairtrade’s projects, programmes, and commissioned studies.

Other tasks that are consistent with the level and responsibilities of this post.

SKILLS REQUIRED

Level of education: The position holder will have a Master’s degree (With a research component) or higher (PhD preferred) in development economics, econometrics, applied sociology, social sciences or another relevant field in management or natural sciences. 

Years of professional experience: A minimum of five years’ experience in research and/or impact evaluations, with at least two years’ experience working on topics relevant to, or with, stakeholders from the Global South.

Job Specific Competencies/knowledge:

- Project Management
- Research and Evaluation
- International Development Expertise
- Stakeholder Management
- Enhancing data-driven decision making
- eLearning Content
- Event/conferences organization
- Capacity Building

Personal Qualities: 

- Cross-cultural communication
- Facilitation
- Rapid Learning
- Collaboration/Teamwork
- Problem Solving
- Multitasking
- Teaching
- Presentation Skills
- Relationship Management
- Evidence Collecting
- Flexibility
- Mentoring

Software/Tools:

- Microsoft 365 (Excel, Word, Outlook, Powerpoint, Teams, Planner, Clipchamp)
- Adobe Creative Cloud & Suite
- Miro
- Canva
- Claude.ai, or similar AI assistant tools

TERMS AND CONDITIONS

- This is a full-time, maternity cover (apprx. until March 2028) position within Fairtrade International.
- Location is at Fairtrade International offices in Bonn, Germany with the opportunity for hybrid work arrangements
- The office language is English.
- Salary as per the Collective Bargaining Agreement for the Wholesale and Foreign Trade Industries for North Rhine Westphalia Group 6a and over tariff payments (starting from 5455,00 Euros gross per month)
- Holiday Bonus and 13th salary  
- 30 days of holidays per year (for full time employees)
- Subsidised public transportation ticket
- Subsidised meal services
- Childcare cost subsidy 

Please note that Fairtrade International is strict on compliance with the required qualification criteria mentioned above, and only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

jobs.occupation: 176/2026 Junior Group Leader (m/f/d) in Computational Multiphase Flow (Ingenieur/in - Verfahrenstechnik)
jobs.description:
The Faculty of Process and Systems Engineering, Chair of Mechanical Process Engineering seeks to fill the following vacancy:

Junior Group Leader (m/f/d) in Computational Multiphase Flow

Salary scale:
13 TV-L

Date commencing:
As soon as possible

Fixed term:
3 years*

Contract status:
100 %

At the Chair of Mechanical Process Engineering (www.mvt.ovgu.de), we are a group of enthusiastic researchers with extensive research activities in the numerical modelling of multiphase flows. Our work addresses the fundamental physical mechanisms governing dispersed and interfacial multiphase flows, as well as their application to engineering systems. Current research topics include particle-laden and droplet-laden turbulent flows, particle–turbulence and droplet–turbulence interactions, the dynamics of non-spherical particles, interfacial flows, and compressible and incompressible multiphase-flow applications. Approximately eight PhD researchers and three postdoctoral researchers currently work in this area at the Chair.

The objective of the advertised position is to attract a junior group leader who will take a leading role in our computational multiphase-flow research. The successful candidate will contribute to and help coordinate ongoing research projects, while also establishing their own research direction within the Chair. The position offers excellent opportunities to develop an independent academic profile and to pursue a Habilitation. It therefore combines scientific leadership in existing activities with the opportunity to initiate new research topics and contribute to the further development of our numerical methods and simulation tools.

Our in-house simulation framework includes state-of-the-art methods for immersed boundaries, Lagrangian particle and droplet tracking, non-spherical particle dynamics, particle and droplet interactions, gas–liquid interfaces, large-eddy simulation, and fully coupled solvers for compressible and incompressible flows. You will also have the opportunity to establish your own teaching portfolio in areas such as numerical methods, multiphase flows, or particle technology.

*The position is full time for a period of 3 years with the opportunity to extend by a further 3 years.

Job description:

- Develop, implement, and analyse analytical and numerical models for multiphase flows
- Establish an independent research profile in computational multiphase-flow modelling
- Lead and coordinate the further development of our in-house simulation tools in C and MPI
- Develop research ideas and prepare proposals for externally funded research projects
- Supervise PhD researchers, postdoctoral researchers, and students working in computational multiphase flows
- Contribute to teaching in multiphase flows, numerical methods, particle technology, or related subjects
- Contribute to the scientific development and coordination of the computational multiphase-flow group
- Opportunity for further scientific qualification, including the possibility to pursue a Habilitation

Requirements profile:

- A Master’s degree or equivalent and a PhD in mechanical engineering, process engineering, aerospace engineering, applied mathematics, physics, or a related discipline
- A strong background in the physical and numerical modelling of fluid-mechanical or multiphase-flow problems
- Demonstrated research experience in computational multiphase flows, such as particle-laden, droplet-laden, or interfacial flows
- Strong scientific-programming skills in C, C++, or Fortran, including experience with MPI and high-performance computing
- Experience in developing numerical methods or simulation software; expertise in techniques such as immersed-boundary methods, Lagrangian tracking, interface-capturing methods, or particle-interaction models is desirable
- A strong publication record commensurate with your career stage, together with the ability to develop independent research ideas and contribute to research proposals
- Excellent written and spoken English, as well as a good command of German or a commitment to acquiring sufficient German proficiency for teaching and administrative duties within two years

For further information about the position, please contact Prof. Berend van Wachem by email, berend.vanwachem(at)ovgu.de

You will benefit from our structures and offerings in the fields of sustainability, diversity, family support and staff development. Our location in the center of a thriving, lively and family-friendly state capital guarantees a high quality of life and a wide range of leisure activities. For more information, please visit www.ovgu.de/en/karriere (http://www.ovgu.de/en/karriere) .

Applications from severely disabled people or people with an equivalent impairment will be given priority in the case of equal suitability, ability and professional expertise. Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg strongly promotes gender equality in all professional areas.

Please send your complete application (motivation letter, curriculum vitae, graduation certificates, references) by October 7, 2026 using the online application portal.
